OpenAI's models: responses, chat, embeddings, audio, images.

## API key

- **Get your key here:** [platform.openai.com](https://platform.openai.com/api-keys)
- **Setting:** `OPENAI_API_KEY`
- **API reference:** [platform.openai.com](https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference)

### Get the key

1. Sign in or sign up at [platform.openai.com](https://platform.openai.com).
2. Add a card and prepaid credits under [Settings → Billing](https://platform.openai.com/settings/organization/billing/overview) ($5 minimum). Turn auto-reload off unless you want it.
3. Open [API keys](https://platform.openai.com/api-keys) and select **Create new secret key**. Owned by **You**, any project, permissions **All**. Your first key asks for a phone number.
4. Copy the key. It's shown once.

### Set it on your Gateway

From your EveryApp folder:

```bash
pnpm everyapp secret set OPENAI_API_KEY
```

It asks for the value at a hidden prompt, and it's live at once, with no deploy. If an app you've installed needs it, `pnpm everyapp configure <app>` asks for it along with everything else the app needs.

To make it the model provider apps get when they ask for the default:

```bash
pnpm everyapp ai default openai
```

### Use it in an app

List it in the app's `everyapp.config.ts`:

```ts
providers: ["openai"],
```

The app calls `/api/ai/openai/…` with `createGatewayFetch()`. More in [AI](/docs/agent/ai).

### Check it worked

- `pnpm everyapp ai list` shows `openai` with its key set, and `pnpm everyapp ai show` says which provider apps get by default.
- `pnpm everyapp status` shows apps that were waiting for it as ready.
